title: WASI throws "memory access out of bounds" when concurrent builds call JS plugin hooks
body:
## Symptom / behavior in Rolldown On the threaded WASI binding (`wasm32-wasip1-threads`), a build randomly traps with `RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds` (stack entirely inside wasm). This is what makes the `wasi / WASI` CI job flaky — e.g. run 32091017370, `fixtures-concurrent.test.ts > external/regexp`. The native binding runs the same suite and never shows it. In Rolldown it shows up when two or more builds run concurrently in one process with a JS plugin hook (e.g. `transform`) active — the wasi test suite's concurrent fixtures with plugins are the usual trigger. That combination is only *how Rolldown reaches the underlying conditions* (concurrent allocation across wasm instances while memory grows); it is not the root cause, and neither the plugin hook nor the concurrency at the build level is fundamentally required — see the root cause below. It surfaces in three shapes, all the same underlying fault: 1. a random test rejects with `RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds`; 2. a test that asserts on an error message gets the OOB text instead (e.g. `expected 'memory access out of bounds' to contain 'Invalid substitution'`) — the trap was caught by the plugin driver and turned into a build diagnostic; 3. mass 60s timeouts / a hung suite — a crashed worker thread is dropped silently (`@emnapi/wasi-threads`' `handleError` only calls `terminateAllThreads()` when the message contains `RuntimeError`/`unreachable`; a bare `memory access out of bounds` worker error doesn't match), so in-flight builds wait forever. ## Root cause **Multiple independent wasm instances share one wasi-libc dlmalloc heap and corrupt it under concurrent allocation when the heap grows.** Under `wasm32-wasip1-threads`, each tokio worker runs in its own Web Worker — its own V8 isolate, its own wasm instance, its own wasi pthread runtime — while all of them share one `WebAssembly.Memory` and therefore one dlmalloc heap (its global state `gm` lives in that shared memory). When instances allocate concurrently and dlmalloc extends the top chunk via `sbrk` (= `memory.grow`), the cross-instance synchronization that should serialize the heap-metadata update (dlmalloc's lock / emnapi's pthread-mutex port) does not hold across separate instances. The shared metadata is corrupted, a later `malloc` returns a bad chunk, and writing into it traps with `memory access out of bounds`. dlmalloc assumes "multiple threads of one runtime"; emnapi hands it "multiple independent instances sharing one heap", and that assumption breaks. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Instance A (Worker isolate)"] B["Instance B (Worker isolate)"] H["Shared dlmalloc heap, gm metadata
in one shared WebAssembly.Memory"] A -->|"malloc, then sbrk = memory.grow, update gm.top"| H B -->|"malloc concurrently"| H H --> R["cross-instance lock not honored,
A and B metadata updates interleave, gm corrupted"] R --> C["later malloc returns a bad chunk"] C --> T["write into it, memory access out of bounds"] ``` The minimal sufficient conditions are three, none of them Rolldown- or TSFN-specific: 1. **multiple wasm instances sharing one heap** (Node's model for wasm threads — one Worker/isolate per thread); 2. **concurrent allocation** across those instances; 3. **`memory.grow` / `sbrk` happening** (the heap climbing past its current top). The JS plugin hook and the threadsafe-function path are **not** required — they are only how Rolldown ends up satisfying (3): each `transform` call wraps a context object whose GC-delayed release makes memory climb, which keeps `sbrk`/`memory.grow` firing. Two pure-wasm controls pin this down: raw `memory.grow` with **no allocator**, multiple instances, one instance touching pages another just grew (even without querying `memory.size`) is **clean** — so V8's cross-instance grow visibility is *not* the fault; but the same wasi-libc dlmalloc under a **single** instance (wasmtime, many host threads) is also clean — so dlmalloc alone is not it either. Only *shared dlmalloc + multiple instances + grow* crashes. Eliminate any one — serialize to one instance, stop concurrent allocation, or stop the growth — and it never happens. Not fixable in Rolldown's own code; the real fix is upstream (napi-rs / emnapi / wasi-libc) — the shared allocator must be safe across instances, or each instance must not share one heap.
Investigation (how the root cause was isolated) A rolldown-free minimal reproducer (~100 lines Rust + a JS driver; napi 3.12.1 + emnapi 2.0.0-alpha.4; `wasm32-wasip1-threads`, debug build) crashes with the same in-wasm OOB within seconds. A single ablation matrix (8-way concurrency, macOS arm64) isolates each factor: | experiment | result | what it shows | |---|---|---| | minimal napi repro: tokio blocking pool + allocation churn (with/without TSFN) | crash in seconds | defect is below Rolldown, in the binding/runtime | | **wasmtime**, pure wasm, wasi-libc dlmalloc, **single instance**, many host threads: 8×400k×256KB | **12/12 clean** | dlmalloc alone is fine — single instance, same allocator, same concurrency | | **pure wasm, raw `memory.grow`, no allocator**, multiple Node Worker instances, one instance touching pages another grew (consumer doesn't even query `memory.size`) | **clean, 8+ rounds** | **V8 cross-instance grow visibility is NOT the fault** | | **pure wasm, shared wasi-libc-style heap, multiple instances** + concurrent alloc + grow | **crash** | shared allocator + multiple instances is the combination | | napi repro, remove grow (allocate-and-free, memory flat) | clean | confirms grow/`sbrk` is the trigger, not instance count alone | The symbolized trap is inside `calloc → __rust_alloc_zeroed → vec::from_elem` on a worker instance — dlmalloc returns a chunk from corrupted metadata and the write into it goes out of bounds. Two controls triangulate the cause: raw grow across instances is clean (rules out V8), single-instance dlmalloc is clean (rules out dlmalloc alone); only shared dlmalloc across instances during grow crashes.
## Related Distinct from #10639 (deterministic post-close trap). ## System info CI: ubuntu-latest, debug wasi build, Node 24.12.0, e.g. run 32091017370 Local: macOS arm64, Node 24.19.0 (V8 13.6), rustc 1.97.1 Reproduces on origin/main cbb8b396e and 64a4b800a (both) — predates #10649 napi 3.12.1 / 3.12.0 · emnapi 2.0.0-alpha.4 / alpha.3 · @napi-rs/wasm-runtime 1.2.3 · @emnapi/wasi-threads 2.0.1
